title: WebSockets
description: Learn how WebSockets enable real-time, full-duplex communication between browsers and servers.

data.text: HTTP was designed for document retrieval. A browser requests a page, the server replies, and the connection closes. For real-time features like chat, live dashboards, or multiplayer games, that request-response cycle is too slow and too inefficient.

WebSockets solve this by upgrading an ordinary HTTP connection into a persistent, full-duplex channel. Once the upgrade is complete, both client and server can send messages at any time without the overhead of new HTTP headers on every message.

A WebSocket connection starts with a standard HTTP request. The client includes an Upgrade: websocket header and a Sec-WebSocket-Key. If the server supports WebSockets, it responds with a 101 Switching Protocols status. From that moment on, the connection is no longer HTTP — it is a raw TCP channel framed by the WebSocket protocol.

data.title: WebSocket Handshake
items: Client sends an HTTP GET request with Upgrade: websocket headers.
Server validates the request and returns 101 Switching Protocols.
Connection is established. Both sides can now send text or binary frames.
Either side can close the connection with a closing handshake.

data.caption: The WebSocket handshake upgrading an HTTP connection.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Browser
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: HTTP GET + Upgrade: websocket
    S->>C: 101 Switching Protocols
    Note over C,S: WebSocket connection open
    C->>S: Text frame: chat message
    S->>C: Text frame: broadcast to room

data.title: Ideal Use Cases
items: Live sports scores and financial tickers

data.title: Consider Alternatives
items: Simple polling scenarios — Server-Sent Events or periodic fetch calls may be simpler.
Very high-scale fan-out — WebSockets require maintaining state per connection, which costs memory and CPU.
Mobile networks with aggressive proxies — some corporate or mobile proxies terminate long-lived connections.

data.content: Open a WebSocket connection and listen for messages.

data.title: Keep Connections Alive
data.text: Load balancers, proxies, and NAT gateways often drop idle connections after 30 to 60 seconds. Always send periodic ping frames or heartbeat messages to keep the WebSocket alive and detect broken connections early.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: WebSockets start with an HTTP handshake and then become a persistent, full-duplex channel.
They eliminate HTTP overhead after the upgrade, making real-time communication efficient.
Use them for chat, dashboards, and live data, but consider connection costs at scale.
data.takeaway: WebSockets are the right tool when your application needs true real-time interactivity, not just faster polling.
